entry_state: Debt balances, cash repayments and risk sensitivities measure different quantities; net borrowing can conceal intraperiod funding. Ownership adds dated share quantities. The split-adjusted basic denominator is established, and potential-share attribution has begun with options and a coupon-bearing convertible; its dilution calculation continues.
exit_state: Ordered dilution uses continuing ordinary earnings and fixed additive instrument effects, preserving unresolved and unsupported cases. Actual conversion creates shares only after exercise and ends the potential-share window. The company example joins tax, journals and shares on the same history. A different initial tax base charges deferred tax to equity; its later earnings consequences remain to be followed.
findings: Preference conversion is excluded after options and debt even though it would pass a comparison with basic EPS. Continuing operations control both profit and loss variants.
The exact ratio derivation relies on positive share denominators and fixed additive effects, not positive earnings. Nonadditive or dependent instruments remain outside its claim.
The early-conversion interpretation is attributed to practice literature separately from IAS32's express maturity treatment. Actual and potential share windows do not overlap.
The company join uses parent-attributed earnings and the matching book. Initial compound tax changes equity and does not supply the later EPS tax addback. No new confirmed defect.
